# Project Aim

The aim of this project is to examine which aspects of early education the school should prioritise to maximise pupils’ development during the kindergarten years and their success throughout the rest of their school career. Specifically, two sub-questions which could be explored are:

1.  *What effects does spending a longer period in kindergarten have on pupils’* *cognitive, social-emotional and executive development, and on their* *functioning in Years 3 and 4?*

In order to examine this question the data will need to contain information pertaining to (a) the amount of years/months children spent in kindergarten, (b) enough variation in terms of how long they spent in kindergarten, to enable a comparison between children who stayed longer, (c) variables that provide information about their cognitive, social-emotional and executive development and lastly (d) information about these pupils that are now in grade 3 or above.

2.  *What effects does a teaching focus on learning objectives aligned with* *Years 3 and 4 have on pupils’ academic achievement and subsequent educational* *pathways?*\
    Will need to be examined in a similar manner.

# Importing Data

Running the code below and loading the data should work if you create a folder named "data" in our repository and copy all the data files into this folder. This folder is in .gitignore so will not be uploaded online but will stay in your local environment.

## 1. Pupils

The pupil data is such that each variable is of the correct type and column names do not contain any spaces. - imported such that the dates are of type date. These are now in the format YYYY-mm-dd. The column names have been changed to contain no spaces. old_name = "new_name"

- Pupil ID = "ID"
- Date of birth = "birth_date"
- Current class = "curr_class"
- Current year group = "curr_year_group"
- Pupil = "pupil"
- Start date = "start_date"

```{r importing pupil data}
# import the pupil data set with the correct data types 
pupils <- read_xlsx(here::here("data", "Pupils.xlsx"),
                    col_names = c("ID", "birth_date", "curr_class",
                                  "curr_year_group", "pupil", "start_date"),
                    skip = 1, # drops the original header row 
                    col_types = c("text", "date", "text",
                                  "text", "text", "date")) |>
  mutate(birth_date = as.Date(birth_date),
         curr_year_group = as.numeric(curr_year_group),
         start_date = as.Date(start_date)) 
        

pupils
```

### Pupil Selection

Firstly, the pupile data provides information about the current group of the pupils. As we need information about how these pupils performed in group 3-4, pupils currently in the startergroup, group 1, and group 2, cannot be included in our analysis. Therefore, pupils currently in group 0, 1, and 2 will be filtered out. After removing these pupils the data set contains 104 entries. The names of these 104 pupils are stored in a vector which will be employed to extract their data from other files.

```{r pupil selection}
# filter out pupils currently in the startgroup, group 1 or group 2 
pupil_selection <- pupils |>
  filter(curr_year_group %in% 3:7)

pupil_selection
```

```{r store pupil names}
# store the names of all the pupils currently in grade 3-7 
pupil_names <- pupil_selection |> pull(pupil)

pupil_names
```

## 2. Observations group 1 and 2

This data file contains observations from students in group 1 and 2. Firstly, the data is imported in the correct format. Secondly, only the rows containing information of the selected pupils above is retained. After filtering the data, this file contains 96821 rows.

```{r importing observation year 1/2 data}
observations_1_2 <- read_xlsx(here::here("data", "Observaties_groep_1_2.xlsx"),
                              sheet = 1, # select only first tab in excel file 
                              col_types = c("skip", "text", "text", "text",
                                            "text", "text", "text", "date",
                                            "numeric", "text", "text", "text")) |>
  mutate(Score = as.numeric(Score), Datum = as.Date(Datum)) # convert type 

```

```{r filter selected pupils}
# only keep data about the pupils as selected above 
observation_selection <-
  observations_1_2 |>
  filter(Leerling %in% pupil_names)

observation_selection
```

# Time spent in Kindergarten

In order to examine how long each pupil stayed in kindergarten, and whether these periods differ enough between pupils to compare between groups, we will need to determine how long each pupil spent in kindergarten.

This could be estimated from the start date of each pupil and the last observation which was made for them in group 1/2. This will not provide a precise estimate but will give us a rough estimation of whether we can proceed.

```{r kindergarden time compution}
# store the date of the first, last and number of observations for each pupil 
last_observation <- observation_selection |>
  group_by(Leerling) |>
  summarise(first_obs = min(Datum, na.rm = TRUE),
            last_obs  = max(Datum, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_obs     = n()) # can check how complete the pupils record is 

# join the days spent in kindergarten to the pupil data 
kindergarten_time <- pupil_selection |>
  left_join(last_observation,
            by = c("pupil" = "Leerling")) |>
  # kindergarten days = last observation - start school 
  mutate(kindergarten_days  = as.numeric(last_obs - start_date),
         kindergarten_years = kindergarten_days / 365) 

kindergarten_time
```

## Robustness Checks

Eyebaling the days spent in kindergarten above indicate there are differences in time spent in kindergarten. However, a few assumptions have been made which need to be verified to ensure this is truly representative of their time spent in kindergarten.

Firstly, the variable start_date has now been interperted as the date at which pupils start school. The following checks will therefore be performed, by computing the number of days between the childs 4th birthday and the start date at school. (a) whether the start_date is after the child's 4th birthday (flag potential mistakes in the data), (b) the child started school no more than 60 days after their birthday (as this school only accepts children that just turned 4), (c) there are no observations before the start date.

Secondly, the time spent in kindergarten has now been estimated from the date at which the last observation was made in grade 1/2 of each pupil. However, if these dates differ significanlty or were registered a long time before the summer holiday (July/ August) we cannot infer how long these children spent in kindergarten. Therefore, the second checks verifies whether the last observation was in july or august (and is not missing).

Thirdly, as a robustness check we can verify whether the pupils current grade year corresponds to the year which they left kindergarten. First by looking at which year the pupil left kindergarten. As school year run from September to August, if the last observation was made between January and August the pupil left kindergarten that year, otherwise the year after. If this calculation is correct, then the expected_end_year should be equal to the end year. Sp for pupils now in grade 4, the end of kindergarten should have been in 2025, and pupils in group 3 2026. e.g. reference year = 2026, current group year = 4 -3 = 1, so ended kindergarten in 2025.

To analyse which pupils fail these checks and why, a table is shown below with which pupils failed which check together with the information which could explain why these checks failed.

```{r}
ref_year <- 2026   # start year of the school year the "current group" refers to

kindergarten_checked <- kindergarten_time |>
  mutate(
    # CHECK 1: start date correct
    days_after_4th_bday = as.numeric(start_date - (birth_date %m+% years(4))),
    check_start = days_after_4th_bday >= 0 &
                  days_after_4th_bday <= 60 &
                  (is.na(first_obs) | first_obs >= start_date),

    # CHECK 2: last observation falls at the end of a school year (May–Aug),
    #          so the notes didn't stop early
    check_last_obs = !is.na(last_obs) & month(last_obs) %in% 5:8,

    # CHECK 3: school year in which kindergarten ended matches the current group
    end_year          = if_else(month(last_obs) >= 9, year(last_obs) + 1, year(last_obs)),
    expected_end_year = ref_year - (curr_year_group - 3), 
    check_group       = !is.na(end_year) & end_year == expected_end_year,

    all_checks_ok = check_start & check_last_obs & check_group
  )

# how many pupils pass each check
kindergarten_checked |>
  summarise(n_pupils = n(),
            across(c(check_start, check_last_obs, check_group, all_checks_ok),
                  ~sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))

# which pupils fail, and why
kindergarten_checked |>
  filter(!all_checks_ok | is.na(all_checks_ok)) |>
  select(pupil, curr_year_group, birth_date, start_date,
         first_obs, last_obs, days_after_4th_bday, end_year, expected_end_year,
         check_start, check_last_obs, check_group)
```

## Interpertation

The table above shows that there are 25 pupils who did not pass the checks. Firstly, of these pupils, 18 are currently in grade 8. These all failed the check verifying whether the last observation in grade 1/2 was in July or August. The last observation of these pupils were all recorded in december. So either their observations got lost or were not stored correctly. As we are examining development in grades 3:4, we could remove pupils in grade 7 all together to ensure that each grade is represented by an equal amount of students. Secondly, two pupils from grade 5 failed because of NAs and one because the first observation was before the start_date. To ensure we have reliable information these pupils will also not be included in the analysis. The remaining pupils who failed the checks were in group 3 and 4. One because if NAs and in every other case because the pupils should have left kindergarten a year earlier than their current group implies. This could be explained if these pupils had to redo year 3 or 4. These pupils will also not be included in further analysis. Leaving us with a total sample size of N = 79.

```{r}
# asked claude how to visualise the distribution 
kg_plot <- kindergarten_checked |>
  filter(curr_year_group %in% 3:6, all_checks_ok) |>
  mutate(kindergarten_years = time_length(interval(start_date, make_date(end_year, 9, 1)), "years"))


kg_plot |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            mean = mean(kindergarten_years),
            sd = sd(kindergarten_years),
            min = min(kindergarten_years),
            median = median(kindergarten_years),
            max = max(kindergarten_years))


ggplot(kg_plot, aes(x = kindergarten_years)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1/12, colour = "white", fill =  "#01665e") +
  labs(x = "Time in kindergarten (years)",
       y = "Number of pupils",
       title = "Distribution of time spent in Kindergarten by the selected pupils", 
       subtitle = "N = 79") 

```

```{r}

#create new column to identify which development function each domain belongs to
observations_filtered <- observations_filtered |>
  mutate(
    development_function = case_when(
     Domein %in% c(
    "Auditieve ontwikkeling",
    "Getallen",
    "Kennis",
    "Proces",
    "Spel",
    "Spelen",
    "Tellen en getalbegrip",
    "Tellen en getallen",
    "Visuele ontwikkeling"
    ) ~ "Cognitive",

      Domein %in% c(
        "De samenleving",
        "Inlevingsvermogen",
        "Interactief taalgebruik",
        "Jezelf en de ander",
        "Ruimte om je heen",
        "Sociaal initiatief",
        "Sociale autonomie",
        "Sociale competenties",
        "Sociale flexibiliteit",
        "Stoeispelen",
        "Welbevinden"
        ) ~ "Social-emotional",

      Domein %in% c(
        "Balanceren",
        "Betrokkenheid",
        "Emotionele competenties",
        "Impulsbeheersing",
        "Morele competenties",
        "Taakgerichtheid en zelfstandigheid"
        ) ~ "Executive",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
observations_filtered

```

```{r}
#calculate the average score from all observations, for each objective, per pupil, per school year
domain_year_scores <- observations_filtered |>
  group_by(Leerling, Jaargang, development_function, Domein) |>
  summarise(
    domain_score = mean(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_observations = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
domain_year_scores

#and now calculate the average of scores per function, each objective receives equal weight by using the objective average here
function_year_scores <- domain_year_scores |>
  filter(!is.na(development_function)) |>
  group_by(Leerling, Jaargang, development_function) |>
  summarise(
    function_score = mean(domain_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_domain = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

function_year_scores
#This includes one row per pupil, per year, per developmental function and the average score in each
#3 functions per year
#1, 2 or 3 years per pupil
```

messy plot, but good to explore the data structure for now
each line represents one pupil, showing for each function how average score changes across the school years

```{r}

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(
  function_year_scores,
  aes(
    x = as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(Jaargang, "^\\d{4}")),
    y = function_score,
    group = Leerling,
    colour = Leerling
  )
) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ development_function, ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(
    as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(
      function_year_scores$Jaargang, "^\\d{4}"
    ))
  ))) +
  labs(
    x = "School year (starting year)",
    y = "Average score",
    title = "Changes in developmental scores for each pupil",
    subtitle = "Each line represents one pupil"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

      TRUE ~ NA_character_

pupils_ok |> count(duration_group)

scores_by_duration <- function_year_scores |>
  left_join(
    pupils_ok |> select(pupil, duration_group),
    by = c("Leerling" = "pupil")
  )
